Defer

dih-FUR -- shares a root with 'transfer' and 'refer,' meaning to carry. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To defer is to submit to another person's judgment or authority out of respect.

On questions of courtroom procedure, even senior lawyers defer to the judge's authority without argument.

Worked Example

Two head chefs disagree about how to plate a dish, but when the restaurant's founder walks in and gives her opinion, both chefs immediately follow her instructions instead.

That willingness to yield to someone else's greater authority or judgment is exactly what it means to defer to them. Unlike 'ignore,' which dismisses another's opinion, defer respects and follows it.

How Defer Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

yield

yield: to give way to another's wishes or authority

submit

submit: to accept the authority or control of another

acquiesce

acquiesce: to accept something reluctantly but without protest

Antonyms

override

override: to use one's authority to reject another's decision

overrule

overrule: to reject a decision using greater authority

How Strong Is It? — yield → defer → acquiesce

yield vs. defer

yield vs. defer: Yield is a bit more general than defer -- yield can describe giving way in almost any contest or pressure, while defer specifically implies respecting someone's greater knowledge or authority.

acquiesce vs. defer

acquiesce vs. defer: Acquiesce can feel more reluctant than defer: defer often shows genuine respect for someone's judgment, while acquiesce can describe going along with something only because resisting seems pointless.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — de-

prefix — de-: away (Latin)

root — -fer-

root — -fer-: to carry, bear (Latin (ferre))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin deferre meant 'to carry away, to refer a matter to someone else,' from de- ('away') and ferre ('to carry'). To defer to someone, at its root, is to carry a decision over to them -- the same root that gives us transfer.

Use the root in a new word: transfer

Use the root in a new word: transfer: The bank can transfer the funds to a new account within one business day.

Word Choice

Defer almost always appears with 'to,' as in 'defer to her expertise,' and specifically describes yielding to someone's judgment or authority on a particular matter.
